title: Zero-error decision within time bound
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let $L$ be a language of finite Boolean strings, and let $T$ assign a natural-number time bound to each natural number. For every input string $x$, the cumulative probability of not having halted, summed over all times, is at most the time bound $T(|x|)$; moreover, every choice string whose run halts produces the one-symbol output indicating whether $x$ belongs to $L$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$L$ is a language of finite Boolean strings
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
the time bound is evaluated at the input length
